question_text: Differentiate between JIT and OJT? In your opinion, which one is better?
Elaborate and defend your favorite experiential method/s used in training and development.
Do you think that the employment relationship is changing in the contemporary world? Comment.
Trace the timeline of development and progression of Human Resource Development as a discipline. Highlight the prominent events that shaped the field.
Elaborate on the employee-dependent factors that affect employee behavior at the workplace.
Elaborate on the processes (any two):

Cummins Engines Company Ltd. (CEC) is a fortune 500 company with its headquarters in Indiana
(US) with an employee base of more than 46,000 and operations in more than 34 countries. CEC has
recently acquired one more location in India (apart from Pune) and is planning to start operations at
the newly acquired site i.e. Gurgaon. The company’s major businesses comprise of developing
powerful tools & motors, vehicle engines (both diesel and petrol), automotives and high-capacity
generator sets. If the company is interested in hiring an HR consultant to hire key personnel and
provide training to them, what kind of training is feasible in this situation. Imagine yourself as that
HRD consultant, take initiative for developing a framework of the proposed training program?
Schematically plan out a feasible and effective training program that would meet the purpose.

HRD professionals at United Technologies Corporation (UTC) would disagree that practice plays an
important role in learning and retention. Visualizing yourself as an HRD professional at Carrier (a UTC
subsidiary), how would you use your knowledge on conditions of practice in training design and what
sort of practice do you think would be most effective for training mechanics in repairing and
troubleshooting problems in air-conditioners. Also, explain the role that trainability might play in the
effectiveness of the HRD program. Do you think that traditional principles of learning (such as
contiguity or association) would be sufficient to train those mechanics? Support your answer.

In your opinion, do you think that managing human resources and developing human resources are
same? Do supervisors have HRD responsibilities? What HRD skills or competencies are required for an
HRD portfolio? What qualities do you think an HRD professional must possess to be effective in an
organization of approximately 1,000 employees? Would you change your response if the organization
on the other hand has 10,000 employees? Do you think that the changing world of work will pose
certain challenges to the HRD professionals in near future. Elaborate your answer with intuition,
insight and relevant examples.

Phyzok Learning Solutions is a Mumbai based startup engaged in personalized and adaptive
learning and content delivery. The company is growing and has become interested in hiring an HR
consultant that will help them in hiring a talented workforce so that they can expand their operations
and services. Do you see that there is a need for training in this situation? What kind of training/s
would be required? What should the HR consultant do to develop a framework of the training
program? Elucidate schematically the steps with special reference to training need analysis (TNA) to
plan out a potentially effective training program. Do you think knowledge of research methodology
will play to your advantage in this situation?

According to recent research, the students in contemporary times are moving away from traditional
learning paradigms and gravitating towards online learning platforms (such as MOOCs, Coursera etc.).
As an end user, what experiences did you have with these innovative learning platforms? Do you
think that technology enabled learning would be better option for learning experiences at both
teaching and training level? Don't you think that traditional learning approaches are irreplaceable?
React to this situation while visualizing yourself as an employee in an organizational context.

Imagine you are Vice President (Learning and Development) of an MNC from the past decade. Your
secretary informed you that a management student (with a dilemma about opting for specialization in
HRD) from a prestigious B-school wishes to meet you for an interview. You oblige the student for the
interview, and when the interview begins after the initial introduction, the student asks a few
questions. The HRD students ask the VP: (1) What do you do here, and what is your role? Is your role
significant? (2) Who are the stakeholders you usually deal with? (3) What is learning and development
in your opinion? (4) Do all employees take an interest and diligently learn? Moreover, 5) What is the
future of the field of HRD? Considering these questions, how would you respond to the student in the
most expressive way possible so that you can justify your position and convince the student to opt for
the HRD specialization?

Visualize the scenario wherein your placements are happening, and the institute is witnessing a
dynamic placement drive. One of the many companies visiting your campus targets the BITSians
aggressively during their recruitment session/s, and the company's representatives deliver
presentations to allure potential employees. In the presentations, the company's HR focuses too
much on some phrases by repeatedly professing that 'we are an Equal Employment Opportunity,
Affirmative Action Employer and we follow KAIZEN". Now imagine that you, as their potential
employee, do not know these phrases; what would you do? Will you ask questions from HR to
elaborate on what these phrases mean? Is it the duty of HR to make you explain the philosophies
behind such phrases, viz. "Equal Employment Opportunity", "Affirmative Action", and "KAIZEN".
Would you want to be part of the selection process if you knew about these philosophies? Would you
change your decision to sit in the interview process if the HR is rude and not explaining what the HR
ought to do? What would be your attitude towards such a company? Also, describe the role of HRD
professionals in managing culturally diverse employees. Articulate your responses by assessing the
situation carefully and justifying your perspective/s.

Suppose your HR Manager asked you to develop an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) proposal.
Which approach would you recommend: an in-house program run by employees of your organization
or a service provided by an outside contractor? Support your choice. Suppose the financial constraints
limit the company from offering only two areas of service (e.g. mental health, substance abuse,
gambling, financial problems). Which services would be most important? How would you assess?
Support your choices. Describe how you would make sure that you select the services that would
provide the most benefits to the company and employees.

What key sectors are highly relevant to the growth and development of any country? These
problems have plagued most developing nations and continue to do the same. With particular
reference to the development scenario in the sectors of health and education, discuss the relevant
strategic interventions, HRD programs and policies that bear the potential to aggrandize the status of
such economies. Elaborate your answer by drawing on the experiential learning of the father of HRD
in India.

Using your knowledge of the stages of life theory of career development, elaborate on how the
career issues of a twenty-eight-year-old differ from those of a fifty-year-old. What would be the
organizational implications of the issues you have identified? Describe how career management can
be viewed as a problem-solving and decision-making process. Explain how organizations and
individuals benefit from a well-defined career management system. Do you see the role of
organizational development processes in aiding the organization's career development programs?

Robert Gagné and others have argued that traditional learning principles (such as
contiguity and association) are insufficient for designing effective training programs. State
the reasoning behind this argument. What does research in instructional psychology and
cognitive psychology offer as a resolution to these problems? Do you agree with this
solution? Support your answer.

Describe the four levels of evaluation that make up Kirkpatrick’s evaluation
Framework. Compare and contrast Kirkpatrick’s original evaluation framework to the
Expanded Kirkpatrick Evaluation Framework presented in the textbook. What is similar,
and what is different about them? Identify one example of data at each level that might be
collected to provide evidence for the effectiveness of a class or training program in which
you have participated.

How do the career issues of a new recruit differ from those of an old recruit? Using
your knowledge of stages of life vis-a-vis career development, explain the predicament of
both categories of workers. Recent research suggests that career plateaus are more
complex than previously thought. Briefly explain why an individual’s perception of being
plateaued is important and how organizations may want to develop multiple ways for
dealing with plateaued employees.

Describe how the skills needed for designing and implementing human process-based
interventions differ from those needed for techno-structural interventions. Is
organizational transformation change a necessity for maintaining an efficient
organization? Why or why not? Even though there is limited empirical evidence to support
organization transformation change intervention strategies, why do organizations still use
this approach? Identify and describe a situation where you think this approach would be
ineffective. Support your answer.

Learners use learning strategies to rehearse, organize, elaborate, and comprehend
new material. From the learning strategies discussed in this chapter, select two that
you have used. For each one, identify how you applied it and how it helped you learn
more effectively.

Why do you suppose the five categories of classroom training are so popular in HRD?
Identify two types of training programs a manager might not want to conduct using a
classroom format.

Describe ways in which career management can be viewed as a problem-solving and
decision-making process.

Given the current trends toward empowerment and employing fewer levels of
management, how important do you believe management development will be in the
next ten years? Support your answer.

Prof. Rao drew inspiration from foreign lands during his attempt to develop human
resources in Indian settings. Mention a few most significant ones for the education
scenario.

Using your knowledge of the stages of life of adult development vis-a-vis career development,
elaborate on how the career issues of a person who has just started his/her career will differ from an
individual who has 15-20 years of work experience. What would be the organizational implications of
the issues you think you would be witnessing while comparing the two individual categories? Elaborate
on the ways in which career management can be viewed as a problem-solving and decision-making
cum strategic process? And, explain how both organizations and individuals can benefit from a well-
defined career management system.

Imagine the situation where you have been working as the General Manager (GM) of a prominent
manufacturing firm that still relies on old methods. Meanwhile, a consultant associated with your
organization very recently suggests that your organization can flourish only if some continuous
improvement methodology is implemented to change the traditional approach. Being a conscientious
GM, what kind of organizational change and development approach would you utilize? How would you
involve maximum stakeholders in this process, and what types of problems would be witnessed for
making such changes? Would organizational transformation change be a more feasible approach for
maintaining the efficiency of such an organization? Why or why not? Use your insights and your
understanding of OD to resolve the situation.

Right from the Independence era to the current period, what all problems have plagued most of the
developing nations from an angle of growth and development? With special reference to the
development scenario in the sector of education, discuss the relevant and strategic interventions,
programs, and, policies that bear the potential to aggrandize the status of such developing economies.
Elaborate your answer by recalling your conceptualization about the constituents of social and
economic development as experienced by the father of HRD in India. In your opinion, how HRD can
HRD to such developmental issues?

Suppose you have been asked to design a program intended to train clerks for the Shipping
Corporation of India(SCI) in the domain of communication. You have been entrusted with the task of
designing, implementing, and evaluating the training program to prove your worth to your immediate
supervisor. What would your strategy be to handle this task given to you? What steps would you be
taking, and what data collection methods do you think would be the most useful in this case? Identify
the training need and describe the process of training which you might design. Once you are done
with the training, what evidence would you give to your supervisor and claim that your training was
effective and efficient? Elaborate using your insights, intuition, and experience.

Robert Gagne and others have argued that traditional principles of learning are not sufficient for
designing effective training programs. What does research in instructional psychology and cognitive
psychology offer as a resolution to these problems? A common stereotype about older workers is that
they find learning difficult. Does research from the field of gerontology support or disprove this
stereotype? Explain. What recommendations or findings do you feel supervisors should follow to
ensure effective training experiences for older workers? Finally, with whatever you have understood
and learned about the field of HRD, come up with your own unique definition of learning.

A mid-sized corporation has decided to conduct a training wherein they are interested
in delivering inexpensive training. They are mainly interested in training managerial staff
who can train newly inducted management trainees. If you were chosen as a consultant by
this organization, what would you do to obtain crucial information about a) the
department or organization’s mission and b) the perceived training needs and suitability of
the training program? Elaborate the process of assessment.

An HRD expert group has developed a contingency model that assumes adult learners
are heterogenous groups requiring different training and development approaches. They
highlight that training and development depend on individual differences. Do you really
think adults and adolescents should be treated differently for training purposes? Do you
see a difference between teaching and training? Elaborate your answer with reference to
your own learning curve.

Beginning from the eighteenth century onwards, trace the historical precursors
informing the field of human resource development. Do you see the role of humans in the
entire idea of HRD? What do they do, and how do they further develop human beings
(employees) in their respective organizations? Do you think the employees’ behavior is
influenced by certain factors? Comment.

Thinking about the COVID times, what experiences have you had with online learning
or training programs? How about technology-enhanced learning, e.g., where a traditional
classroom also uses online discussions or other web-based applications? In your view, how
can technology best be used to provide effective training and learning opportunities? Do
you think online training is really effective? If yes, are there any specific contexts where
online training can be effective? Comment.

Using your knowledge of the stages of life (Erikson's theory in particular) and career development,
elaborate how the career issues of a 25 year old will differ from a 50 year old individual. What would
be the organizational implications of the issues you have identified? Describe the ways in which career
management can be viewed as a problem-solving and decision-making process? And, explain how both
organizations and individuals can benefit from a well-defined career management system.

Imagine that immediately after IAS probation training you have been assigned to the ministry of
civil aviation. On the second day of your office, you are given the charge of Air-India and you are
appraised of the deteriorating condition of the government run business. On the third day of your job,
you have been asked to analyze the problem and overcome the issues by the civil aviation minister
himself. Further assume that the ministry has given you full authority and autonomy to devise the
most feasible strategy to overcome the continuous losses and making the entire business move
toward profitability. Considering the situation at hand, what approach would you use? How would
you move ahead to assess and improve the situation at hand? Deliberate as to what would you do to
change the face of the business?

Suppose that you are the recruitment manager for a medium sized bank. One of your best
recruiters appears to be unmotivated lately. The number of new recruits the recruiter brings in is
normally above average for effective performance, but recently it has fallen below the standard for
the past two weeks. Considering this scenario, what do you suppose, what might have gone wrong
with the employee's performance? Are their any theoretical frameworks which can come to our
rescue and can help the employee in question? What recommendations would you provide to help
improve that employees' performance? Is it possible to help him/her at a personal level as well?

Visualize the scenario that your placements are scheduled anytime soon. One of the many
companies visiting your campus has put banners during their recruitment session and their
representatives deliver presentations to allure BITSians. In their presentations, they focus too much
on their primary strength by professing that 'we are an Equal Employment Opportunity and
Affirmative Action Employer'. Considering the fact that they are a US based MNC, compare and
contrast the philosophies of 'Equal Employment Opportunity' 'Affirmative Action' and "Managing
Diversity'. What would be your attitude towards such a company? Also, describe the role of HRD
professionals with respect to managing culturally diverse employees? Articulate your responses by
assessing the situation carefully and justifying your perspective/s.

Imagine the situation where you have been working as the General Manager (GM) of a prominent
IT/ITES organization. Meanwhile, a consultant associated with your organization suggests that your
organization can flourish only if some sort of continuous improvement methodology is implemented in
a timely manner. Being a conscientious GM, what kind of organizational development intervention
approach would you utilize? How would you involve entry level and seniormost executives in this
process and what types of problems would be witnessed by you for making such changes? Do you
think organizational transformation change would be more feasible for maintaining the efficiency of
such organization? Why or why not? Use your insights from the understanding about OD to skillfully
resolve the situation of the GM.

Imagine that you are heading the Learning and Development team in a multinational firm for the
past decade. You come to know today that a management student with specialization in HR from a top
B-School (who is doing his/her project on HR practices in your firm) seeks to meet you for your
interview. When s/he comes to take your interview after your consent, s/he asks you three questions,
namely;
i) What do you do?
ii) What challenges have you faced during the past five years? and,
iii) Where do you see the HRD field in the next five years?
How would you respond to these interview questions in the most expressive way possible, so that, you
can justify your position to that HR student and justify your specialization?

With reference to your conceptualization about the constituents of social and economic
development, what are the key sectors that are highly relevant as far as the growth and development
of any country is concerned? What problems have plagued most of the developing nations from this
angle. With special reference to the development scenario in the sector of education and health,
discuss the relevant and strategic interventions, programs and policies that bear the potential to
aggrandize the status of such developed economies.

You have been assigned to design a program intended to train airline flight attendant trainees
during emergency evacuation procedures. You are now required to design the evaluation study to
show that the flight attendants understand the procedures and use them on the job. Which data
collection methods do you think would be the most useful in providing this evidence? How might a
type of learning outcome affect your choice/s of how to measure learning happened in this case?
Identify and describe at least three et

hical considerations when conducting evaluation research. Do
you see a similarity in the research process required to assess training needs and evaluate training
designs? Comment.
